children: In an effort to generate additional revenue to help fund its robotaxi, robotics, and AI ambitions, Chinese automaker Xpeng
plans to offer its technology stake to other carmakers besides partner Volkswagen
for ~$700M, giving the company access to Xpeng’s
EV platform, software, and electric architecture.
is now putting those systems out for bid to other interested partners, including software developers and automobile suppliers.
To facilitate the search for new partners, Xpeng
established a strategic commercialization team six months ago, taking cues from its Volkswagen

partnership, sources cited by Reuters said. Its technology partnership with Volkswagen—along with the sale of components and accessories—has proven to be extremely profitable, as services and “other businesses” revenue nearly doubled in the second quarter, driving a 2,150 expansion in the segment’s margin.
During the company’s most recent earnings call, CEO He Xiaopeng noted the profitable opportunities in robotics and commitment to making investments to further the goal of commercialization.

“The lifetime revenue and gross profit contribution of each IRON [humanoid robot], including hardware sales and recurring revenue from upgrades to AI model capabilities, will be substantially higher than the average selling price and gross profit per vehicle of our automotive business.”

“To accelerate the commercialization of physical AI, we recently established a group-level business development team within the group and are actively engaging with the partners in China and overseas to bring our industry-leading Turing AI chips, VLA 2.0, robotaxi, and humanoid robot technologies to global markets more quickly,” He added.

title: Xpeng to offer tech systems to foreign parties to fund robotics, robotaxi ambitions -- Reuters
